findings.title: A GM's notice of a ruling card with no thread carries the card's buttons, unwired: Allow, Refuse, Spring the trap, Rearm and Choose the target again in the notice only close it
findings.surface: A GM's notice of a ruling card with no thread
findings.control: The card's buttons as copied into the notice
findings.where: scripts/popup.mjs:1267-1269 and 1287-1298 (the notice drawn from the words whole), 1072-1077 (a click anywhere closes it); scripts/call-gm.mjs:976-986 (gmPopup on the no-thread road); against scripts/messenger-app.mjs:617-625 (cardPreview takes the buttons off the messenger's notices)
findings.what_happens: callGm's road with no thread (gmOnly, or a character with no player) whispers the card to the GMs with gmPopup, so popup.mjs raises it for every GM. It hands showPopup the words as they are, and a GM's copy of the words keeps .drpg-call-actions (secret.mjs strips them for a player only). Nothing wires a button inside a notice: wireCallActions runs on a bubble and on the chat log's render alone. The press bubbles to the card's click, which closes the notice as read. The messenger's own notices were fixed for exactly this (the comment at messenger-app.mjs:610-616: 'every button on one looked live and did nothing at all') and the no-thread road was not.
findings.failure_scenario: In an Eclipse a GM gets the notice 'A ruling to make' for Chie's Direct Murder, presses 'Allow on Strength' in it: the notice closes, nothing is ruled, and the card in the chat log still waits for a ruling.
findings.expected: the notice carries no buttons (as cardPreview does) or its buttons open the card where it can be ruled
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a wiring of [data-drpg-call] inside .drpg-popup: wireCallActions' callers are messenger-app.mjs:684 (a bubble) and gm-bridge.mjs:157-158 (renderChatMessageHTML, the log) only. Looked for a stylesheet rule that hides .drpg-call-action in a notice: none among the 356 rules naming the notices' and cards' selectors. Checked that a GM's words keep the buttons: secret.mjs:325-329 ('A player is sent the words without the two blocks now; a GM gets them as written'). The three posters with gmOnly are GM-side: traps.mjs:323-348, eclipse.mjs:685-700, projects.mjs:1465-1471. The notice history's snapshot keeps no button (SNAPSHOT_TAGS, notice-history.mjs:203-205), so only the live notice is wrong. old-1.2.42-comms COMM-02 (fixed) reads the popup's flags and the log's wiring, not the notice's buttons; scenario 30 7l2 reads the flags. No test presses a button inside a notice.
findings.probe: as a GM: arm a watched trap, walk a student into its room so traps.mjs posts the alert; on the GM read #drpg-popups .drpg-popup .drpg-call-action (expected 0, read 2), press [data-drpg-call=fireTrap] in it and read whether the murder window opened and the card in the log settled

findings.title: A ruling card that finds nothing to rule on gives its buttons back and says nothing: an item handed over leaves a creative-use card no button can close, Refuse included; a deleted character does the same to most cards; a Call's or a Dynamic action's ask the primary dropped is told in the console only
findings.control: Works: apply an effect / Works, no effect / Refuse; Approve (a Call); Set the difficulty / Refuse (Dynamic); Reply, Nothing was there, Refuse the attempt, Give an existing item, the project's Refuse
findings.where: scripts/messenger-app.mjs:939-941 (the item read before any branch), 783 (hold(false), nothing said); 1132-1133, 1186-1187, 1212-1213, 1290-1291, 1057-1058, 1356-1357, 1378-1379, 1430-1431 (if (!actor) return null); 862, 881, 886 with scripts/call-gm.mjs:476-484, 500-508 (warn, utils.mjs:333-336: the console)
findings.what_happens: Every handler that returns null tells wireCallActions the ruling was not made: the claim is dropped and the buttons come back (messenger-app.mjs:778-783), with nothing on screen. For the creative-use card the item is read at 940-941, before the itemRefuse branch at 943, so when the item is no longer on the character - handed over (inventory.mjs:1187-1200 deletes the last piece), stolen, destroyed by a Call - all three buttons do nothing. ruleCreativeUse's own 'gone' answer (settled 'nothing to rule on', 960) is reached only when the item goes during the window. The card has no expiry (use-items.mjs:596-609). The same early return on a deleted character holds every button of the generic cards. A Call's Approve and a Dynamic's two buttons answer false when the primary holds no such ask, and the GM sees the buttons come back.
findings.failure_scenario: Bob asks whether his odd spoon works, then hands the spoon to Chie before the GM looks; the GM presses Refuse on Bob's card, the buttons flash and come back, nothing is said, and the card reads 'Awaiting a ruling' for the rest of the campaign.
findings.expected: a card whose subject is gone settles with the 'nothing to rule on' line (DRPG.Items.rulingGone exists) or says why it cannot be ruled; a Call or Dynamic button the primary refuses says so on the GM's screen
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for anything that settles or ends a creative-use card when its item leaves: nothing in use-items.mjs, inventory.mjs transferItem or the card's poster; the card has no expires, so sweepAskCards (call-gm.mjs:207-218) never ends it. Tier 2 E14-T7 covers a busy item, one used up (broken, still there) and one stashed during the window, all of which reach ruleCreativeUse; none deletes the item before the press. For the Call and Dynamic case: the primary's own resend road (askAgain, call-gm.mjs:150-163) re-holds an ask when the asker resends after a reload, and expiry ends the card at its time, so that silent window is short; kept as part of this finding, not on its own.
findings.probe: as a player: use a Tier 0 item creatively; as the GM, hand the item to another student (inventory.mjs transferItem); press [data-drpg-call=itemRefuse] on the card; read cardFlag(message, 'settled') and any notice shown

findings.what_happens: Every GM gets a notice of a thread's ask ('Waiting on your ruling'). When one GM rules it, settleCall writes the card's words again and every bubble and the log redraw; the notices on the other GMs' screens are copies and are reached only by a deletion or an overruled Objection's mark. findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another closer of notices: only trial.mjs:702 (the overruled stamp's own) and the deletion hook dispatch drpg-dismiss. watchCard observes the notice's own body, not the message. The notice is a copy by design (popup.mjs:16-21); the owner's rule of 20.11.2026 is what makes the copy's staleness a finding. The click still opens the conversation, which is right.

findings.title: The notice history's list waits for the reader: new entries behind a pill while the list is scrolled or holds focus, a change to drawn entries until focus leaves it

The list is held while the reader is in it, so a row that was settled or marked deleted keeps its old tags until focus leaves the list, and a new card is behind 'Show new notices'. The A7 design (P10) chose this so the list does not jump under the reader; the standing rule of 20.11.2026 names 'redraws only after focus leaves' as what it does not want.

findings.expected: the owner's call: the A7 design or the 20.11 rule
findings.refutation_tried: A recorded design choice, not a defect of the code (the comment at 357-362). Filed as nit so the owner can weigh it against the new rule.
